title: The European Supervisory Authorities designate critical ICT third-party providers under DORA
date_evidence: Digital Finance and Innovation 18/11/2025 The European Supervisory Authorities (EBA, EIOPA, and ESMA - the ESAs) publish today the list of designated critical ICT third-party providers (CTPPs) under the Digital Operational Resilience Act (DORA).
key_claim: Acting jointly through the Joint Committee under Article 31(9) of DORA, the EBA, EIOPA and ESMA published the first official list of designated Critical ICT Third-Party Providers, bringing those providers under direct EU-level oversight that assesses their ICT risk-management and governance frameworks.
notes: Canonical Tier 1 designation event and the spine of the signal -> used as the single permitted structural anchor. Dated 18 Nov 2025, within the 12-month anchor allowance. Companion EIOPA page carries identical text and links the official list PDF.

title: UK and EU regulators sign Memorandum of Understanding to strengthen oversight of critical third parties
key_claim: The FCA, Bank of England and PRA signed an MoU with the EU's European Supervisory Authorities to coordinate and share information on oversight of critical third parties under the UK CTP regime and CTPPs under the EU's DORA - including during incidents such as power outages or cyber-attacks - with the UK designation process having begun.
notes: First formal cross-border coordination of cloud/ICT-supplier oversight between the EU and UK regimes; mirror EU-side release at ESMA (14/01/2026).

title: Supervisory priorities 2026-28: charting a course through turbulent waters
date_evidence: meta-article:published_time: 2026-01-22 ... '22 January 2026' 'By Sharon Donnery, Member of the Supervisory Board of the ECB, and Mario Quagliariello'
key_claim: The ECB's 2026-28 supervisory priorities make operational resilience and ICT capabilities a top priority, with particular attention to cybersecurity and third-party risk management, and call on banks to swiftly implement DORA's new third-party requirements.
notes: Fresh in-window Tier 1 showing the central-bank supervisor elevating ICT third-party (incl. cloud) risk.

title: PS7/26 - Operational resilience: Operational incident and third-party reporting
verbatim_quote: Respondents supported the proposed alignment of reporting requirements with international practice and standards such as the EU Digital Operational Resilience Act (DORA) and the Financial Stability Board's (FSB) Format for Incident Reporting Exchange (FIRE).
key_claim: The PRA's final policy on operational-incident and material-third-party reporting will give the PRA better oversight of risks arising from firms' use of third parties and support identification of critical third parties and assessment of where critical nodes of failure could arise, with reporting deliberately aligned to the EU's DORA regime and the FSB's FIRE standard.
notes: Tier 1 primary UK regulator source (PRA, with FCA and Bank of England as FMI supervisor); final policy statement following CP17/24, feeding the UK CTP regime and interoperable with DORA.

title: DORA CTPP Oversight: What It Means for Cloud Providers and Major Vendors
date_evidence: meta-article:published_time: 2026-02-03T00:00:00Z ... 'The Lead Overseer can issue recommendations but cannot directly impose binding orders or fines'
verbatim_quote: The Lead Overseer can issue recommendations but cannot directly impose binding orders or fines.
key_claim: Counter-position: DORA creates a first-of-its-kind EU-level direct-oversight framework for cloud hyperscalers, but the Lead Overseer cannot directly impose binding orders or financial penalties - enforcement is indirect (public notices; recommending that financial entities suspend or terminate the provider) - and underlying cloud concentration risk persists because genuine substitutability is limited and migration takes 12-18 months.
notes: Counter-position source (specialist cyber-assurance advisory, Tier 2). Argues the new powers are weak/indirect and that concentration risk persists regardless.

title: TSC publishes Regulator responses to its report on AI in Financial Services
date_evidence: meta-article:published_time: 2026-04-20T13:48:34+00:00 ... 'On 16 April 2026, the Treasury Select Committee (TSC) published Reponses from HM Treasury (HMT), the Bank of England (BoE) and Financial Conduct Authority'
key_claim: The Treasury Select Committee recommended HM Treasury designate the major AI and cloud providers as Critical Third Parties by the end of 2026; HMT responded that it is gathering evidence and 'expects to make initial designation decisions this year' (2026).
notes: Freshest in-window UK development (reporting the 16 Apr 2026 TSC publication); confirms political pressure to bring hyperscalers into the UK CTP perimeter. Law-firm-published trade blog (Tier 3).

title: DORA CTPPs explained: rules, risks and obligations
date_evidence: meta-article:published_time: 2026-05-05T14:44:49+00:00 ... 'On 18 November 2025, the ESAs published the inaugural official list of designated CTPPs under Article 31(9) of DORA. The 19 companies span a wide range of services'
key_claim: The 19 designated CTPPs - including Amazon Web Services, Google Cloud and Microsoft - are now supervised directly by the ESAs as entities in their own right rather than through their financial-institution clients, with persistent non-compliance punishable by periodic penalties of up to 1% of average daily worldwide turnover per day of breach under Article 35(6).
notes: Freshest in-window specialist trade-press explainer; lists all 19 CTPPs and articulates the perimeter-extension framing. Tier 3.
